# NHL Scores & Stats Dashboard

### A full-stack hockey platform for following NHL games and exploring player and goalie performance.

[![Live Demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/Live_Demo-Open_Dashboard-003E7E?style=for-the-badge)](https://hockey-scores.vercel.app)

## Overview

The NHL Scores & Stats Dashboard brings game results and player performance data into one focused experience. Users can follow current and recent games, compare skaters and goaltenders, and narrow large datasets through search, team filters, sorting, and pagination.

I built the project to explore full-stack API integration with live sports data. It combines a component-based Angular interface with an Express service that normalizes data from external hockey sources and exposes consistent endpoints to the client.

## Core Features

- **Current and recent games:** Display NHL matchups, team logos, scores, start times, and live-game status.
- **Player statistics:** Explore skater performance with searchable and sortable statistical tables.
- **Goalie statistics:** Review goaltender performance through a dedicated filtered view.
- **Team filtering:** Focus results on a selected NHL team without manually searching through the full dataset.
- **Pagination and sorting:** Navigate larger player and goalie datasets while controlling the displayed metric and order.
- **Protected accounts:** Register, sign in, validate sessions, and restrict dashboard routes with JWT-based authentication.
- **Resilient game display:** Fall back to the latest available NHL game when no recent matchup is returned.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Angular Client] --> B[Express + TypeScript API]
    A --> C[ESPN Scoreboard API]
    B --> D[NHL Stats API]
    B --> E[(MongoDB)]
    B --> F[JWT Authentication]
```

The Angular client owns navigation, protected routes, score cards, statistics tables, filtering, sorting, and pagination. The Express backend retrieves and normalizes NHL statistics while managing user registration and authentication. MongoDB stores account data, and signed JWTs protect authenticated application routes.

## Technical Decisions

- Used **Angular standalone components** to organize score, player, goalie, login, and registration experiences.
- Centralized the backend base URL in an **Angular environment configuration** for local and deployed environments.
- Normalized different external player-name formats in the API before returning data to the frontend.
- Used **RxJS and Angular HttpClient** for asynchronous requests and view updates.
- Added client-side search, team filtering, sorting, and pagination to make large statistics datasets easier to explore.
- Protected application routes with an Angular authentication guard and validated sessions through the Express API.
- Kept game-score and statistical data separate so each external source could serve the workflow it supports best.
